What Greek term in Hebrews expresses the absolute unrepeatability and definitive sufficiency of Christ's sacrifice?
column2:
Ephapax (ἐφάπαξ) — "Once for all" (Heb 7:27; 9:12; 10:10).

🧠 Mnemonic: EPHA-PAX: An EPHEMERAL once-and-done offering on Calvary that guarantees eternal PAX (peace) with God. No sequels required!

column1: Why could Jesus not be a priest under the Mosaic Law according to Hebrews 7:14?
column2:
Because Jesus belonged to the tribe of Judah, whereas the Mosaic Law strictly reserved the priesthood to the tribe of Levi (Aaron's descendants).

🧠 Mnemonic: JUDAH RULES, LEVI PRIESTS: Judah wears the royal crown; Levi wears the priestly ephod. Christ the King from Judah must belong to a different order: Melchizedek!

column1: According to Hebrews 7:16, Christ is constituted priest not according to a legal prescription of carnal descent, but according to what?
column2:
According to the power of an indestructible life (secundum virtutem vitae insolubilis / dynamis zoēs akatalytou).

🧠 Mnemonic: AKATALYTOU = NON-CATALYSIS: His priesthood does not dissolve or decay with age like Aaron's, but flows from the inextinguishable life of the eternal Son.

column1: What two biblical Old Testament texts establish the Messiah as Priest according to the order of Melchizedek?
column2:
1. Genesis 14:17–20 (Melchizedek brings bread and wine, blesses Abram)
2. Psalm 110:4 ("Tu es sacerdos in aeternum secundum ordinem Melchisedech").

🧠 Mnemonic: GENESIS 14 BRINGS BREAD, PSALM 110 SINGS IN AETERNUM: Abraham receives bread and wine in Gen 14; David hears the eternal priesthood decree in Ps 110:4.

column1: How does the author of Hebrews (Heb 7:7–10) demonstrate that Melchizedek's priesthood is superior to Levi's?
column2:
1. Abraham paid tithes to Melchizedek and was blessed by him.
2. The lesser is blessed by the greater.
3. Since Levi was still in the loins of his forefather Abraham, Levi symbolically paid tithes to Melchizedek.

🧠 Mnemonic: LEVI IN THE LOINS TITHES FIRST: The lesser is blessed by the greater. Levi was still genetic seed in Abraham's loins, so Levi bowed and paid tithes to Melchizedek!

column1: What are the two essential poles of the definition of the priest in Hebrews 5:1?
column2:
1. Solidarity ("taken from among men" / ex hominibus assumptus) — capacity to co-suffer (sympathein).
2. Transcendence ("appointed on behalf of men in relation to God") — divine call rooted in filiation (Ps 2:7).

🧠 Mnemonic: SOLID ROOTS, TRANSCENDENT ANCHOR: Taken from men (sympathy in our dirt); Appointed by God (anchor in the Trinity). The priest is a bridge touching both shores.

column1: Why did the Council of Trent (Session XXIII) establish an inseparable bond between Priesthood and Sacrifice?
column2:
To dogmatically prove the existence of the New Testament ministerial priesthood against Protestant denials of the Eucharistic sacrifice, not to reduce the priesthood to a mere functional ritualism (sacrificator).

🧠 Mnemonic: EXISTENCE, NOT EXHAUSTION: Trent proved Orders truly EXISTS against Protestant denial; it did not reduce the priest to a ritualistic slot-machine.

column1: In what way does the sacrifice of Christ radically differ from Old Testament and pagan sacrifices regarding the victim?
column2:
In Christ, the Offerer and the Offering are identical: Sacerdos et Victima (the synthesis of sacrificial action and sacrificial passion).

🧠 Mnemonic: THE SHEPHERD BECOMES THE LAMB: Unlike Aaron who slaughtered external beasts, Christ is simultaneously the Hands that offer (Sacerdos) and the Body on the altar (Victima).

column1: What is the fundamental Christological binomial used by Vatican II (LG 28; PO 2) to structure the theology of Holy Orders?
column2:
Consecration and Mission (Consecratio et Missio, based on John 10:36: "the one whom the Father consecrated and sent into the world").

🧠 Mnemonic: CON-MIS COMPASS: Consecration gives the spiritual engine; Mission gives the steering wheel. You cannot be sent without fuel, nor fueled without moving.

column1: What is the ontological ground of Christ's role as the one Mediator between God and men (1 Tim 2:5)?
column2:
The Hypostatic Union (Perfectus Deus, Perfectus Homo) uniting the ascending mediation (homo ad Deum) and descending mediation (Deus ad homines).

🧠 Mnemonic: TWO NATURES, ONE BRIDGE: The Hypostatic Union is the bridge itself. God cannot suffer; man cannot redeem infinitely. In Christ, God redeems through human flesh.

column1: Did the sacraments of the Old Law confer sanctifying grace ex opere operato?
column2:
No. They operated ex opere operantis / ex fide as professions of faith (protestatio fidei) in the future Passion of Christ (St. Thomas Aquinas, ST III, q. 62, a. 6).

🧠 Mnemonic: PROTESTING FAITH, NOT PRODUCING GRACE: Old Law rituals were a promissory note (protestatio fidei) looking forward to Calvary; New Law sacraments cash the cheque ex opere operato!

column1: Why did the justified Old Testament patriarchs remain in the Limbus Patrum until Christ's death?
column2:
Because the objective price of redemption (pretium redemptionis) had not yet been historically paid on Calvary; the gate of heaven (ianua caeli) was opened only by the Cross and the Descensus ad inferos.

🧠 Mnemonic: TICKET PURCHASED ON CALVARY: The ancient just had true faith, but the toll price (pretium redemptionis) was only paid on Good Friday; until then, the turnstile remained locked.

column1: What Patristic axiom of Tertullian did Prof. Zaccaria cite to explain why the Holy Spirit always acts through bodily realities (Incarnation, imposition of hands, celibacy, male reservation)?
column2:
Caro cardo salutis ("The flesh is the hinge of salvation").

🧠 Mnemonic: FLESH IS THE DOOR-HINGE: The Latin 'cardo' is a door hinge; salvation swings on physical hinges (Incarnation, physical hands on heads, baptismal water, male bodies).

column1: In Exodus 24:1–8 (ratification of the Sinai Covenant), what two liturgical elements prefigure the bimodal structure of the Christian Mass?
column2:
1. Reading the Book of the Covenant (prefiguring the Liturgy of the Word).
2. Sprinkling the Blood of the Covenant (prefiguring the Liturgy of the Eucharist). Note: mediated by Moses, who was not a temple priest!

🧠 Mnemonic: SINAI SCRIPTURE & SINAI BLOOD: Moses reads the Book (Liturgy of the Word), then splashes the Blood (Liturgy of the Eucharist). The Mass follows the Sinai covenant blueprint!

column1: According to Prof. Zaccaria, how does the Old Testament Levitical concept of holiness contrast with Christ's priestly mediation?
column2:
1. Old Covenant (Levitical): Holiness as progressive separation from the profane and from death (e.g., Priest and Levite avoiding the half-dead man in Lk 10).
2. New Covenant (Christ): Mediation through total solidarity with sinners right into death (Heb 2:10; 5:8–9).

🧠 Mnemonic: LEVI FLEES DEATH; CHRIST EMBRACES IT: The Levitical priest avoids dead corpses to protect ritual purity (Good Samaritan); Christ touches lepers and enters the tomb to obliterate death from within.

column1: How does Catholic theology answer the objection that celebrating Mass daily contradicts the ephapax / semel ("once for all") character of Christ's sacrifice in Hebrews?
column2:
The Mass does not multiply or repeat Calvary; it renders sacramentally present the one, identical historical sacrifice (same Victim, same Priest, same sacrifice) so that objective redemption may be applied subjectively in time and space.

🧠 Mnemonic: PROJECTOR, NOT REMAKE: The daily Mass is not a movie remake or sequel of Calvary; it is the identical historical film projected onto today's screen across the world.

column1: What are the 4 defining characteristics of Christ's sacrificial oblation highlighted by Prof. Zaccaria?
column2:
1. Purpose (Scopo): Not to appease an angry God, but to unite us to the Father's will.
2. Content (Contenuto): Identity of Priest and Victim (Sacerdos et Victima, no animal substitution).
3. Modality (Modo): Primacy of interior filial love/obedience over mere physical pain.
4. Trinitarian Dynamism: Offered in the Holy Spirit ("il Donato ridonato").

🧠 Mnemonic: SPOM: Scopo (filial reunion), Persona/Contenuto (Sacerdos et Victima), Obbedienza/Modo (love over pain), Movimento Trinitario (offered in the Holy Spirit).

column1: What are the 5 characteristics of Christ's priesthood secundum ordinem Melchisedech taught in Lecture 1?
column2:
1. Superior to the Levitical priesthood (Abraham paid tithes & was blessed by him).
2. Permanent/Ontological (intrinsic to Christ's person, not a temporary phase).
3. Universal (for all peoples/times, not bound to a tribe).
4. Of Divine Initiative (by vocation, not biological birth).
5. Unique & Eternal (in aeternum).

🧠 Mnemonic: SPUD-U: Superior to Levi, Permanent/Ontological, Universal scope, Divine call (vocation), Unique & eternal (in aeternum).

column1: How does the unicity of Christ's priesthood differ from the unity of the Old Testament Levitical priesthood?
column2:
1. Levitical: An institutional unity fragmented across thousands of individual mortal priests.
2. Christ: A strictly personal unicity (One Priest, one Sacrifice) in which ministerial priests participate sacramentally.

🧠 Mnemonic: RELAY TEAM VS SOLO MONARCH: Levi is a fragmented relay team passing the baton across dead runners; Christ is the sole eternal High Priest whose priesthood never changes hands.

column1: According to Prof. Zaccaria, is it the quantity of physical suffering or the nails per se that saves us on the Cross?
column2:
No. What saves us is Christ's filial obedience (repairing Adam's disobedience, Rom 5:19; Phil 2:8) as the supreme historical manifestation of unconditional love. Love is the cause; obedience is the vehicle.

🧠 Mnemonic: FIAT NOT FLOGGING: Physical torture alone does not atone. The saving power is the infinite love driving the Son's obedience ('Fiat voluntas tua') conquering Adam's pride.

column1: Why does the liturgy use oil for consecratory anointing rather than water?
column2:
Unlike water which dries and is wiped away, oil penetrates deeply and cannot be removed. It permanently marks the subject, signifying that the Holy Spirit penetrates the deepest ontological core of the person and remains definitively (sacramental character).

🧠 Mnemonic: WATER DRIES; OIL SINKS: Water evaporates off the skin; oil penetrates into the pores forever. Orders is not a temporary wash, but an indelible seal on the soul.

column1: What is Christ's gratia capitalis (capital grace), and why is it essential for soteriology and sacraments?
column2:
It is the grace Christ possesses as Head (Caput) of the Mystical Body and firstborn among many brethren. Because of gratia capitalis, Christ possesses corporate humanity (umanità corporativa), meaning what happened to His human nature (death, resurrection) touches and transforms us when united to Him.

🧠 Mnemonic: WHEN THE HEAD SWIMS, THE BODY CROSSES: Christ is the Head (Caput). Because humanity is bound to Him as His mystical body, His victory over death pulls all baptized members through with Him.

column1: How do the names "Jesus" and "Christ" encapsulate the conciliar binomial of Holy Orders?
column2:
• Jesus (Yeshua = "God saves"): His Mission (ontological Missus a Patre).
• Christ (Christos = "Anointed"): His Consecration (by the Spirit in the Hypostatic Union).

🧠 Mnemonic: JESUS = MISSION (Yeshua: God saves); CHRIST = CONSECRATION (Christos: Spirit-anointed). Inseparable like His Two Natures.
